title: Scalar transport of localization triangles and the open unit
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $E,L/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite extensions, $m,n\ge1$, $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$, $B=\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^n$, and $\varphi:A\to B$ any unital map [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On each scheme $T$ use constant module sheaves on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and write $S_T^{A,B}K=K_B=K\otimes_A^LB$ for uncompleted derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The notation $D^b_{ctf}$ means bounded constructible with finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. All schemes below are separated and finite type over $k$; all scheme maps are $k$-maps [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the constructible exceptional functors and their adjunctions on bounded constructible inputs of etale origin [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and ordinary derived direct images [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be closed, $j:U=X\setminus Z\hookrightarrow X$ its complementary open, and $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$. Put $N_A=Ri_A^!M$ and $N_B=Ri_B^!M_B$. Suppose $M_B$, $(N_A)_B$ and $N_B$ lie in their respective $D^b_{ctf}$ categories and $N_A,j_A^*M$ have bounded constructible etale origins of finite Tor amplitude. Then $U$ is Noetherian and $j$ is quasi-compact, separated and finite type. The following are distinguished triangles in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$ [def-weil-triangulated-category]:
$$S_Xi_{*,A}N_A\xrightarrow{S_X\epsilon_{i,A,M}}M_B\xrightarrow{S_X\eta_{j,A,M}}S_XRj_{*,A}j_A^*M\longrightarrow,$$
$$i_{*,B}N_B\xrightarrow{\epsilon_{i,B,M_B}}M_B\xrightarrow{\eta_{j,B,M_B}}Rj_{*,B}j_B^*M_B\longrightarrow.$$
Here $\epsilon$ is the exceptional counit and $\eta$ the ordinary $j^*\dashv Rj_*$ unit, with the adjoint $Ri^!$ identified with the constructible exceptional functor, and $S_T=S_T^{A,B}$. The ordinary coefficient comparisons $c_{i,N_A}:S_Xi_{*,A}N_A\to i_{*,B}S_ZN_A$ and $c_{j,j_A^*M}:S_XRj_{*,A}j_A^*M\to Rj_{*,B}S_Uj_A^*M$ are isomorphisms in $D(B)$, with exactly the counit-transpose normalization of [lem-coef-finite-direct-image]. Let $r_{j,M}:S_Uj_A^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}j_B^*S_XM$ be the canonical tensor restriction comparison, and set $d_{j,M}=Rj_{*,B}(r_{j,M})c_{j,j_A^*M}$. Then
$$d_{j,M}\,S_X(\eta_{j,A,M})=\eta_{j,B,M_B}.$$
This is equality of the specified morphisms in $D(B)$, without a flatness assumption.

proof.text: Apply finite type over a Noetherian field directly to both X and U, using their given structure morphisms, and combine local Noetherianity with compactness. The Noetherian target makes the open immersion j quasi-compact. Open immersions are separated and locally of finite type.

Reuse the adopted source library implementation of the finite stage of localization, in WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.ProEtale.FiniteCoefficient.Derived.LocalizeConstructible, rather than the unfinished all-stage package. The intrinsic realization equivalence translates the constructibility hypotheses to fixed-module bounded constructibility. An exponent annihilating each coefficient ring is invertible in k: k has characteristic p by the cardinality of its finite base field, and ell differs from p. The source localization theorem gives the triangle for the ambient support adjoint. Construct the comparison to the prescribed exceptional functor from the natural Hom equivalence, using the images of identities and its inverse; naturality proves the two inverse equations. The inverse-transpose formula, followed by the proper lower-shriek/lower-star comparison, proves the exact counit equation. Transport the ambient triangle along the resulting pushed-forward isomorphism. Do this at A and B. Restriction of scalars is an exact functor induced on derived categories, hence triangulated; its left adjoint has the induced shift comparison and is triangulated by the Mathlib adjunction theorem. Apply this left adjoint to the A-triangle, including its shift comparison in the connecting arrow.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1: tensor the support triangle; use the already established finite localization theorem

proof.text: The ring $B$ is a finite $A$-module: its finite set of elements is a finite generating set. The hypotheses supply bounded constructible etale origins of finite Tor amplitude for $N_A$ and $j_A^*M$. The schemes are finite type over $k$, and Step 1 verifies the separated finite-type hypotheses for $i,j$. Hence the pro-etale clause of the finite direct-image theorem, applied to $(i,N_A)$ and $(j,j_A^*M)$, gives exactly $c_{i,N_A}$ and $c_{j,j_A^*M}$ as isomorphisms in the $B$-coefficient categories. Its specified transpose is the scalar-extended ordinary counit; no flatness of $A\to B$ is used. Closed direct image is exact by [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact], since Step 1 verifies its quasi-compact-complement hypothesis; thus its derived direct image is the termwise $i_*$ used here.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: the third term and the ordinary coefficient comparisons

proof.text: Use the fixed-module scalar/pullback comparison in ProEtaleFixedScalarRestrictionDirectImage. Its reverse is an iterated mate of the restriction/pullback square. The iterated-mate/conjugate equivalence identity identifies the conjugate of this reverse with the fixed restriction/direct-image comparison. Applying the inverse equivalence and taking inverse isomorphisms identifies it with finiteClosedScalarPullIso, exactly the isomorphism in the statement. The defining finite direct-image coefficient map is the right mate of the forward comparison.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: normalize the open restriction comparison and its direct-image mate

proof.text:
The unit-mate identity at $M$ now reads
$$c_{j,j_A^*M}\circ S_X(\eta_{j,A,M})=Rj_{*,B}(\lambda_M)\circ\eta_{j,B,S_XM}.$$
Postcompose with $Rj_{*,B}(r_{j,M})$. Functoriality gives $Rj_{*,B}(r_{j,M})Rj_{*,B}(\lambda_M)=Rj_{*,B}(r_{j,M}\lambda_M)=1$ since $r_j=\lambda^{-1}$. The left side becomes $d_{j,M}S_X(\eta_{j,A,M})$, and the right side is $\eta_{j,B,M_B}$. This is equality of the specified morphisms in $D(B)$; the cancellation uses an isomorphism of pullback functors and does not tensor an ordinary exact sequence or assume coefficient flatness.
